question_text: If a = 2i+3j+4k, b = i+j−k and c = i−j+k, then compute a×(b×c) and verify that it is perpendicular to a.

recall_prompt: Say how you would compute this and then check it is perpendicular to a.
formula_note: a×(b×c) is perpendicular to a for ANY vectors a, b, c, not only for this particular set — a cross product is always at right angles to its first factor. The dot-product check here confirming zero is not a coincidence of these numbers; it will hold every time this construction is used.

steps.why: a×(b×c) is a combination of b and c, and crossing anything with a leaves a result perpendicular to a. The dot product is the check that turns that fact into a marked step.
common_mistakes: Taking a cross product instead of a dot product.

insider_note: b×c has a zero i component, which is a help rather than a sign of error. The verification is a DOT product with a, and it must be shown to come to 0 explicitly.
